newsitem.title: USA: Kasich, at Iowa fund-raiser, considers run in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Kasich, at Iowa fund-raiser, considers run in 2000.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich, speaking at a Republican fund-raiser in the key presidential primary state of Iowa, said he will have laid the groundwork for a presidential bid by late 1999 if he expects to run in the year 2000.
"I'm travelling all over the country. I'll be going around now as I write my new book," Kasich told a news conference.

"Next year, it'll be a full year of campaigning for my colleagues so I clearly will have been in enough places to determine my own destiny after the '98 election," he told more than 1,000 Republicans at the state's spring GOP fund-raiser.
The Ohio Republican, who has crusaded for a balanced budget throughout his eight terms in Congress, is considered a top contender for the Republican nomination in 2000.

Iowa Republican chairman Steve Grubbs said Kasich did not currently have a cadre of supporters or a "ground crew" to launch a presidential campaign in the state, which hosts the nation's first presidential caucuses.

But Grubbs added, "After tonight he's going to know a thousand people in Iowa. The thing about Congressman Kasich, when you see him live, when you see him give a speech, you can't walk away and not be motivated and want to go out and work for your country. If he wants to run for president, after tonight I am convinced he'll have a volunteer base out there ready to go."
Kasich, who hails from Columbus, Ohio, will run for re-election to Congress in 1998, and he told Iowans he feels "compelled" to talk about how the Republican party can "save our culture."

Kasich praised the 1960s activism of the Baby Boom generation: "We were good examples, not bad examples, of the fact that people can make a difference and we need to rekindle the spirit, that it isn't government that's going to do it ... but it's up to each and every one of us to heal that part of the world in which we work and live."
